$comment: §4.1c mutation coverage for every rendered VERDICT and every rendered
MEASUREMENT in this lab. One entry per marker, of either family: a
data-verdict marker says what happened, a data-claim marker is a number the
reader is invited to check, and a number painted with no mutation behind it
is exactly as unchecked as a verdict painted with none.
A mutation counts as a KILL only when the unmutated baseline PASSED in the
same run, the failure is that marker's OWN assertion (not a build error, a
blank page, a timeout, or the whole suite going red), and the run served the
mutated code. mutations/run.mjs enforces all three; it runs with CI=1 so
playwright.config.ts's reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI is false and no
stale server on port 4667 can answer for an unmutated checkout.
e2e/verdicts.spec.ts fails if the page renders a marker of either family
that this file does not cover, fails if this file claims a marker the page
never renders, and fails if a recorded kill's test does not go through the
shared helpers (expectVerdict / expectNoVerdict / readClaim) — a spec that
merely mentions a marker id is not a spec that asserts it. A marker
reachable only on a failure path carries rendersOnlyUnderMutation: true, and
the spec then requires it to be ABSENT from the healthy page, so the flag
cannot be used to hide a verdict that really does render.

mutations.grep: KAT strip verdict follows the measured vectors
mutations.why: Corrupts the FIPS 197 C.1 expected vector so one of three KATs fails. The strip must then say 'Known-answer mismatch' with data-state='fail' and 2/3.
mutations.scope: Also reddens claims.spec.ts's negative-claim test, which legitimately asserts green KATs; the kill is recorded from the marker's own test via --grep.

mutations.grep: headline advantage and ledger are independently consistent
mutations.why: Severs the IND-CPA verdict from the measured Wilson interval. Textbook RSA with re-encrypt wins every trial, so the verdict must read BROKEN: ADVANTAGE.

mutations.grep: negative claim survives green KATs and two misleading flat lines
mutations.why: Pins the negative-fixture headline AND its tone to the placeholder state, so two genuine flat lines no longer promote it to the 'AND THE SCHEME IS BROKEN' form.

mutations.replace:
const schemes = await createSchemeRegistry();
    throw new Error('mutation: forced scheme-registry failure');
mutations.grep: healthy boot renders no engine-failure verdict
mutations.why: Forces the catch branch that paints the engine-failure verdict, proving that banner is reachable and that the healthy-boot assertion can see it.
mutations.scope: Exhibit 01 never initializes, so this mutation is panel-global by construction; the marker's own test races the two outcomes so the failure is an assertion, not a timeout.

mutations.grep: exact CCA challenge is refused and hidden panels stay unpainted
mutations.why: Makes the oracle-boundary verdict stop reporting the real byte-comparison refusal; it must flip to BOUNDARY FAILURE.

mutations.grep: CCA2 verdict follows the measured interval
mutations.why: Severs the CCA2 verdict from its measured interval. ElGamal malleation wins every trial, so the alarm branch is the only correct one.

mutations.grep: forgery verdict follows the real verifier outcome
mutations.why: Inverts the EUF-CMA verdict's tone branch, so a real textbook-RSA forgery renders as a pass and a refused RSA-PSS alteration renders as an alarm.

mutations.grep: ECDSA values reconstruct the accepted high-S twin
mutations.why: This is the mutation that exposed the original defect: the plain verifier now REJECTS the (r, n - s) twin, collapsing exhibit 03's whole point. Before this lane the banner was a literal and all ten claims stayed green while the page rendered 'PLAIN VERIFIER: ACCEPTED' beside a computed 'rejected'.

mutations.replace: return secp256k1.verify(signature, message, publicKey, { lowS: false });
mutations.grep: ECDSA values reconstruct the accepted high-S twin
mutations.why: Drops canonical low-S enforcement, so the 'library default' verifier accepts a high-S signature. The banner must follow it to ACCEPTED; the test decides the expected outcome from arithmetic on the displayed s, not from the page.

mutations.grep: switching verdict follows the measured rows
mutations.why: Severs the sampler verdict from the measured rows, so the banner cries SAMPLER CHECK FAILED while every displayed row sits inside bound + tolerance.

mutations.grep: reduction verdict follows the measured factor
mutations.why: Severs the reduction verdict from the measured Adv(B) vs Adv(A)/2 comparison, so it reports RELATION OUTSIDE while the displayed numbers agree.

mutations.grep: the coin claim shows the bit the transcript opened
mutations.why: Paints the opposite face on the opened coin, so the coin and the transcript line that names the same bit disagree.

mutations.grep: the CPA advantage claim equals the recomputed Wilson estimate
mutations.why: Renders the interval floor where the point estimate belongs, so the readable number stops being the Wilson estimate of the rendered ledger.

mutations.grep: the CPA interval claim equals the recomputed Wilson interval
mutations.why: Collapses the interval onto its upper end, so the displayed width no longer reports the sampling uncertainty it claims to.

mutations.grep: the CPA ledger claim balances against its own trial count
mutations.why: Puts the complement in the wins tile, so wins + losses + errors stops equalling the trials the same ledger reports.

mutations.grep: the CPA rate claim equals the win and loss shares of the ledger
mutations.why: Labels the win bar with the loss share, so the histogram disagrees with the ledger it summarises.

mutations.grep: the CCA2 ledger claim balances against its own trial count
mutations.why: Puts the loss count in the wins tile, so the CCA2 ledger stops balancing against its own trial count.

mutations.grep: the CCA2 advantage claim equals the recomputed Wilson estimate
mutations.why: Halves the machine-readable advantage, so the value a tool reads is no longer the value a reader sees, nor the estimate of the rendered ledger.

mutations.grep: the CCA2 interval claim equals the recomputed Wilson interval
mutations.why: Collapses the CCA2 interval onto its upper end, so its displayed width no longer reports the sampling uncertainty it claims to.

mutations.grep: ECDSA values reconstruct the accepted high-S twin
mutations.why: Drops the leading digit of every transcript value, so the numbers the reader is invited to check no longer reconstruct the curve order or the (r, n - s) twin.

mutations.grep: the switching rows claim matches the bound recomputed at the chosen n
mutations.why: Doubles the rendered switching bound, so the column stops being q(q - 1) / 2^(n + 1) at the n the control is set to.

mutations.find: svg.setAttribute('aria-label', `Measured PRP/PRF advantage and switching bound for ${points.length} query counts from ${points[0]!.queries} to ${points.at(-1)!.queries}.`);
mutations.replace: svg.setAttribute('aria-label', `Measured PRP/PRF advantage and switching bound for ${points.length} query counts from ${points[0]!.queries} to ${points[0]!.queries}.`);
mutations.grep: the switching chart claim spans the same points as the table
mutations.why: Makes the chart's only screen-reader rendering claim a span it did not measure, while the table beside it still shows the real one.

mutations.grep: the scaled bound claim equals
mutations.why: Turns q(q - 1) into q^2 in the n = 128 rescaling, so the formula the page prints beside the curve is not the formula it names.
mutations.scope: --grep is a regex, so this record names a metacharacter-free substring of the test title rather than the whole title, which contains q(q - 1).

mutations.grep: the reduction A claim renders one measurement two ways
mutations.why: Separates the readable A advantage from the machine-readable one, so the two renderings of one measurement stop agreeing.

mutations.grep: the reduction B claim renders one measurement two ways
mutations.why: Separates the machine-readable B advantage from the readable one, in the other direction from the A mutation.

mutations.grep: the reduction relation claim is half the measured A advantage
mutations.why: Breaks the displayed Adv(A) / 2 factor away from the displayed Adv(A), which is the one relation this exhibit exists to show.
